reviews.comment: His class was the toughest I had so far at A&M after 2 years, but he was the best prof I had at A&M. Whatever he was doing radiate his love and care for the class and individual students that I enjoyed the class even when it was tough. He will accomplish great things in the future. Best wishes to him!
Where are you, Toshi? That's how much I loved and miss his class. I realized it a lot more after the fall semester started. Great prof and wish he teaches more at A&M.

Even though his final sucked my soul up, he made the class doable and the lectures enjoyable. While he presents himself a justice guy, he gives extensions when I needed. Actually he reached out to me to check on me and asked me if I wanted to complete assignments I missed. A&M should have kept him around but Australia is lucky to have him.

Toshi creates a classroom you actually want to be in—even if the course sucks—something I haven't seen another professor pull off. He's funny, “strict,” but incredibly fair. Even though his handwriting sucks haha, he truly cares. He'd reply to my emails within minutes at 11 p.m. or 6 a.m.

His final was hard but he told us about it ahead of time. While I was nervous about the final for a while, I was also excited to come to his class everyday. He gets us and show tremendous care to individual students. We will miss him at A&M. Australians are blessed to have him!

Honestly, I understand why someone said Toshi is GOAT. He sounded strict at first, but he is really reasonable and flexible. He makes us take accountability, but in a very kind way. It is only about a half way through the summer, but so far I have enjoyed his class over the other that I decided to drop.

I've never thought of actually learning materials from an online course. Prof Toshi is amazing and caring. He spent a lot of time to customize the course a lot. Communications were quick and clear too. His lecture videos and study guides helped me understand the materials and set me up for success. I recommend him to any students.

Professor Fukui is an amazing Professor. By far the best professor out of all the businesses minor classes. His lectures ensure you understand the content. His final is very challenging (more so than the midterms and quizzes). However, he deeply cares about his students and their success. I am very grateful for Professor Fukui.

I have heard a lot of horrible thing about FINC 409 from others but it was a lot better experience than I expected with Prof Toshi. I believe he went above and beyond what he was expected by school to make his own lecture videos and align his assignments/quizzes/exams with his teaching style. Even though I did not get an A, I actually enjoyed it.

I was not expecting this level of care from an online course professor. He went more than above and beyond with the course. I have a friend taking the same course from another professor, but it sounds very different. Prof Toshi made his lecture videos, study materials, quizzes/exams, which made the course smooth in my opinion and helped me learn.

The course was very straightforward and the professor made it easy to understand. Lecture videos and study guides are available for all exams and they really help a lot. The extra credit is easy and the professor even gave a major curve with an 86 and above counting as an A. He really cares for his students and helps them in all the ways he can.

This class is the first and the last class that I actually enjoyed learning out of all business related classes I had to take for business minor. He created his own lecture videos with examples that are relatable to the real world. He communicates frequently and replies his emails promptly. If he is not the best, one of the top professors at A&M.

A great prof who showed extra care to his students despite being an online course. Exams were tough but he made his own lecture videos, study guides, etc. He went above and beyond any professors I know even though he is a PhD student. I can say I actually learned the materials instead of studying for my grade. Recommended if you care your learning.

I took his online finance class, but he must be better in person. His videos were very good, and the homework aligned well with the quizzes. BUT the tests were super difficult and the average on the final was a 66, which he said was "very good." I put in a lot of work and prayers into this class, and I would not put myself through it again.

Even though we have never met him in person since this is an online course, he seems like a great professor. He created his own videos to go through concepts with examples, gave us study guides that he made, and made things clear. His expectations are clear. Unlike what I have heard about this course and the instructors, he went above and beyond.
Toshi is the G.O.A.T.

Professor Toshi was one of the kindest professors I've ever had. The course is slightly difficult but he is reasonable. I really loved that he went out of his way to not only teach us finance topics but also real-world information to help his students throughout life. I would highly recommend taking him over other professors for this course!

Coming into my third year at A&M, I had never had a professor like Prof Toshi. His not just knowledgeable, but extremely caring as if he is watching each student individually despite him having 150 students. He is an animated lecturer with jokes and illustrates the concepts of finance with real-world examples, which helped me love finance. SUPER!

Toshi was the best professor I have ever had at Texas A&M. He expects a lot and his class is probably the toughest I have ever had. However, the grades came out fair, I believe. He thought the class with a good amount of examples. It was his first time teaching, so I am sure he will make some adjustments. An extraordinary professor.

A great professor and the best finance professor I have ever had at A&M so far. While he put a clear line between students and him, I felt closer and more comfortable communicating with him than any other professors. Exams are not easy, and he expects out of us a lot, but it was one of the best learning experiences I had at A&M. Highly recommended!
